definitions.explanation: A small lizard that clings to walls and windows with its toes and comes out at night to eat insects. Common on Japanese houses, where it is welcomed as a guardian of the home.

examples.english: There's a gecko on the window.
Geckos are said to protect the house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{明|あ}かり→明かり：01681_akari⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{集|あつ}まる→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧⟦{虫|むし}→虫：02262_mushi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ヤモリ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}てくる→出てくる：29121_detekuru⟧。
examples.english: On summer nights, geckos come out to eat the insects gathered around the lights.

notes:
The kanji spellings {家守|やもり} and {守宮|やもり} reflect the old belief that the gecko guards the house, and many people will not harm one for that reason.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦イモリ→イモリ：30980_imori⟧: newt — an amphibian living near water; the pair are often confused, and a saying contrasts ⟦イモリ→イモリ：30980_imori⟧ ({井守|いもり}, well guardian) with ヤモリ ({家守|やもり}, house guardian)
- トカゲ: lizard — the general word, for ground-dwelling lizards
